question: Rifampicin reduces the contraceptive efficacy of combined oral contraceptive pills (OCPs) by inducing CYP3A4, thereby accelerating oestrogen and progestogen metabolism and lowering their plasma levels.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true and clinically very important. Rifampicin induces CYP3A4 (and other enzymes), accelerating breakdown of oestrogen and progestogens in OCPs. This is a pharmacokinetic drug interaction leading to contraceptive failure.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Rifampicin is one of the most potent CYP3A4 inducers known. It significantly increases OCP component metabolism, reducing plasma levels by up to 60–70%. Women prescribed rifampicin must use additional/alternative contraception during treatment and for one month after stopping.
